Why it exists

A view count means nothing without the creator’s normal.

Half a million views is a hit for one creator and a flop for another. The useful question is how a video did against what that creator usually gets.

Most tools that answer it charge $15 to $99 a month. I built Rank Kiwi for myself because I refused to pay a subscription just to see which videos beat a creator’s median. It scans the Reels or videos on the page, works out the median, and shows how many times each one beat it.

How it works

  1. 1

    Open any creator

    An Instagram Reels tab or a YouTube channel’s videos.

  2. 2

    Scan what’s on the page

    Rank Kiwi gathers the view counts and works out the median.

  3. 3

    Sort by outliers

    Spot the 3× to 10× spikes and export them to a spreadsheet.

What it does

Built for Short-form creators, video editors, YouTubers, channel strategists, social media managers and agencies doing competitor research.

  1. 01

    Outlier score

    Views divided by the creator's median. Breakouts float to the top, whatever the channel size.

  2. 02

    YouTube scanner

    Benchmarks long-form videos and Shorts against the channel median and sorts by multiplier.

  3. 03

    Reels insights

    Engagement metrics for Reels on Explore and creator profiles.

  4. 04

    One-click export

    Excel or CSV, or paste formatted rows straight into Google Sheets, Notion or Airtable.

  5. 05

    Reel transcripts

    Turns spoken audio into timestamped or plain-text transcripts with your own Groq key.

Inside the product

Decisions that shaped it

Median, not average
One viral post drags an average up and makes everything else look weak. The median is the creator’s real normal, so a score of 3× means the same thing on a small channel and a huge one.
It runs in your browser
There is no login and no password to hand over. The extension reads what is already on the page you opened.
Free, with no paid tier
It was built to avoid a subscription, so it does not have one.
Export first
Research ends up in a spreadsheet anyway. One click gives Excel or CSV, or rows you can paste into Google Sheets, Notion or Airtable.
